text:
aya: Heads up — Okta alert: sudden spike in MFA push prompts across ~12 users, 27 failures from 198.51.100.47 in last 8m. Looks like push-bombing.

okta-bot: [Alert] Unusual Auth Activity
- Type: MFA_FAILURE_RATE
- Count: 27
- Source IP: 198.51.100.47
- Geo: Netherlands
Link: https://okta.example/alerts/abc123

jordan: Are any of the users org-admins or service accounts?

aya: Two devs and one infra service account (infra-deploy@redwood). No org admins.

samir: Block the IP at the edge and revoke sessions for the infra service account. Also rotate its key if it's a machine key.

security-oncall: Acknowledged. Blocking IP now and revoking sessions for listed accounts. @aya can you paste the list?

aya: Users: jordan, maria, akash, infra-deploy@redwood. Also one test account test-ci.

infra-bot: Firewall rule created: block-ip-198-51-100-47 applied to edge-lb (id: fr-9456)

security-oncall: Revoked all Okta sessions for infra-deploy@redwood and forced password reset for affected human accounts.

okta-bot: Action log: sessions_revoked for infra-deploy@redwood by security-oncall at 2026-03-20T14:05:42Z

maria: FYI — test-ci is a known flaky CI account, can exclude from user comms. Any evidence of credential compromise?

samir: Checked CloudTrail & Okta admin logs — no suspicious KMS decrypt activity, no console logins with admin role. Looks like MFA push fatigue rather than credential theft.

leo: Please create an incident and notify affected engineers. Suggest temporary require-password change + enable WebAuthn for org.

aya: I'll open the incident and draft the all-dev note. Also adding audit logging for MFA challenge outcomes to our telemetry dashboard.

jordan: Can we add a short-term rate limit on MFA push challenges to prevent this attack vector? Who owns that config?

security-oncall: Rate limiting on push challenges is in Okta policy — I've opened a ticket with identity to enable stricter rate limits and block unknown Geo. ticket: ID-3421

maria: Postmortem items: 1) Enable push rate-limiting 2) Exclude service accounts from push MFA, prefer key-based auth 3) Add automatic session revocation playbook. I'll add those to the incident.

aya: Thanks — no further alerts after block. Marking immediate containment done. Leaving follow-ups in the incident.

security-oncall: Closing thread for now. If you see reattempts from new IPs ping here.
